newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depos, swaps softer in light late dealing.
newsitem.headline: Greek depos, swaps softer in light late dealing.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards slipped lower in light late dealing with little action in the overnight and the central bank draining overnight surplus liquidity at an unchanged 12.4 percent.
"It was a quiet day with not a lot of interest. We had a little action in the overnight. Depos and swaps dipped again by around 10 basis points" said a money market dealer.

Purchases of FRNs auctioned on Monday were settled on Wednesday, meaning that 325 billion drachmas of o/n money left the system. But dealers said there were still surplus funds and the Bank of Greece stayed on the bidside in the overnight.
On Monday, Greece auctioned 250 billion drachmas of seven-year floaters with the first coupon set at 14 percent on Monday, October 21.
The average price was a touch above par, 100.001475. The minimum accepted price was 99.9211, the highest 100.25. The floaters mature October 2,3 2003.
The spread was held constant at 150 basis points but the benchmark 12-month T-bill was cut by 20 basis points to 12.50 percent. The latest one-year T-bill rate was 12.70 percent.
The mark was quoted at 156.53/56 drachmas from Wednesday's 156.600 fix, the dollar at 238.12/22 drachmas from 238.700 and the Ecu at 300.20/25 from 300.240 drachmas.
"There were sales of 100 million ecus at the fixing which gave rise to an inflow of about 25 billion drachmas," a dealer said.
